A_general.open_code_note: No public Krisp MCP repository or package was found in the collected evidence. The endpoint is documented as a hosted server; no code was available to compare with its deployment.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: MCP is listed as a Core plan integration, and the MCP documentation lists Core and Advanced plans as eligible. The sources do not state a separate MCP charge.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The pricing page lists Core at $16/user/month monthly or $8/user/month annually, Advanced at $30/user/month monthly or $15/user/month annually, and Enterprise at custom pricing. It also lists a free seven-day trial.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Krisp's pricing page states per-user monthly and annual prices for Core and Advanced. It does not state a separate MCP per-call or credit price.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The supported-tools page says Core and Advanced plans and any user role (Admin, User) can use the feature. Access is OAuth-protected and subject to the user's workspace permissions.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor plan eligibility and OAuth; the user's Krisp workspace permissions also bound access.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: OAuth discovery is documented using RFC 9470 and RFC 8414; MCP protocol version is not stated.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint returned HTTP 401 without a bearer token and advertised protected-resource metadata at https://mcp.krisp.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource. That document names https://mcp.krisp.ai as authorization server. Its authorization-server metadata advertises authorization_code, refresh_token, and urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange; S256 PKCE; client_secret_basic and client_secret_post at token and introspection endpoints; and a registration endpoint. Authorization-server metadata scopes_supported: user::me::read, user::meetings::read, user::meetings:notes::read, user::meetings:transcripts::read, user::meetings::list, user::meetings:metadata::read, user::meetings:metadata::write, user::subscriptions::read, user::subscriptions::write, user::activities::list, user::kagent:phone-numbers::read, user::kagent:phone-numbers::write, user::kagent:calling-platforms::write, user::kagent:telephony-providers::read, user::kagent:telephony-providers::write, user::kagent:termination-trunks::read, user::kagent:termination-trunks::write, user::kagent:secrets::read, user::kagent:secrets::write, user::kagent:agents::read, user::kagent:agents::write, user::kagent:agents::publish, user::kagent:agent-branches::read, user::kagent:agent-branches::write, user::kagent:audit-logs::read, user::kagent:kb::read, user::kagent:kb::write, user::kagent:tools::read, user::kagent:tools::write, user::kagent:integrations::read, user::kagent:integrations::write, user::kagent:auth-stages::read, user::kagent:auth-stages::write, user::kagent:auth-profiles::read, user::kagent:auth-profiles::write, user::kagent:api-providers::read, user::kagent:api-providers::write, user::kagent:webhooks::read, user::kagent:webhooks::write, user::kagent:sessions::read, user::kagent:sessions::write, user::kagent:sessions::interact, user::kagent:analytics::read, user::kagent:analytics-registry::read, user::kagent:analytics-registry::write, user::kagent:analytics-reprocess::write, user::kagent:judges::read, user::kagent:judges::write, user::kagent:judges::publish, user::kagent:eval::read, user::kagent:eval::write, user::kagent:eval::run, user::kagent:voice-profiles::read, user::kagent:voice-profiles::write, user::kagent:access-tokens::read, user::kagent:access-tokens::write, user::kagent:custom-vocabularies::read, user::kagent:custom-vocabularies::write, user::recording::import. C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The endpoint requires Authorization: Bearer <access_token>; docs say tokens are validated by OAuth2 token introspection. The docs describe refresh when a refresh token is returned.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE (S256), refresh_token and token-exchange grants advertised, client_secret_basic/client_secret_post token and introspection authentication methods, and dynamic registration endpoint https://mcp.krisp.ai/.well-known/oauth-registration. Token lifetime and revocation are NOT FOUND. The protected-resource metadata scopes_supported list is recorded in description_what_how; authorization-server scopes_supported also includes broad kagent and subscription scopes.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official documentation identifies six workspace-changing tools: attach_tag, detach_tag, complete_action_item, complete_action_items, bulk_update_speakers, and import_recording. It publishes no MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint). 2. The server docs recommend client-side human confirmation for write calls; no server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval step is documented. 3. OAuth scopes are documented in C. Docs say access follows the user's workspace permissions; the supported-tools page says Core and Advanced plans and any Admin or User role. Redirect-URI approval, token lifetime, and revocation are not documented. 4. A single endpoint is documented; no readonly mode, toolset filter, environment selector, or regional endpoint is documented. SSE is unsupported. 5. Meeting access is bounded by workspace access. The tools can return transcript content and participant details where available; no MCP-specific masking or PII exclusion is documented. 6. Document IDs are 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Search terms need at least 3 characters; get_multiple_documents supports up to 50 meetings for lightweight content and a handful for notes/full transcripts; upcoming meetings cover 1–14 days; a meeting holds at most 7 tags; imports accept listed audio/video formats up to 1 GB and should be started one at a time. 7. The docs specify ID format and some input constraints, but do not publish schemas or describe general unknown-argument rejection, coercion, aliases, or server overrides. 8. MCP request logging and MCP-specific audit trails are not documented. The security page describes Krisp employee access monitoring for meeting transcripts, not MCP-call auditing. 9. The 18 official tool names/descriptions contain no feedback, rating, report, survey, or vendor feedback action. No MCP upsell result is documented. 10. The supported-tools page gives usage guidance, while setup guidance recommends client-side confirmation and trusted clients; these recommendations are not documented as server-enforced. 11. No agent-behavior memory is described. Workspace mutations such as tags and action-item status persist in the product. 12. The input is one hosted endpoint with one documented tool list; no sub-server or dynamic toolset architecture is documented. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, or script-execution tool appears in the official tool list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official supported-tools page lists 18 tools and has no stated total. All 18 official names are in actions.json. No catalogue-only tools were added. Claude's connector directory lists 7 names, a subset of the official 18. MartechDB reports 18 tools. Other reviewed catalogues did not provide an additional verified native tool list.

actions.description: Search meetings and return metadata, summaries, key points, and action items.
Search transcripts, agendas, and notes for matching passages.
Fetch selected meeting documents and requested content, including full transcripts.
List action items with assignee, due date, status, and source meeting.
Mark one action item done or reopen it.
Mark up to 50 action items done or not done.
List or search meeting folders and their metadata.
Get folder details and its meetings.
Add tags to one or more meetings; creates missing tags.
Replace transcript speaker labels with names; updates transcript and summary.
Import an audio or video recording as a new meeting.
Check status of a recording import.
List calendar meetings for the next 1–14 days.
List Activity Center updates, newest first.
Read display preferences such as name, timezone, and company.
Get current date/time or enumerate dates in a range.

E_aggregated.token_method: No public code or verbatim complete tool definitions and initialize instructions were available to compute a token estimate.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The product offers many non-MCP functions, including noise cancellation, accent conversion, meeting recording controls, account/team and billing management, administrative controls, integrations, and webhooks. The reviewed MCP list does not expose these as tools. The pricing page describes product functions; the MCP supported-tools page defines the available MCP actions.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The vendor recommends human confirmation for six write tools and warns about untrusted clients: “Keep human confirmation on in your AI tool so you can review those calls before they run.” This is client-side advice; the docs do not describe server-enforced confirmation.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Krisp states that access follows workspace permissions and recommends trusted clients. Its security page says meeting notes/transcripts are encrypted with restricted access and that user data access is monitored. It also says meeting transcripts and summaries belong to the user and describes hard deletion when users delete them. Its pricing page states meeting data is not used to train Krisp AI models.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes the server as hosted and using OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, and says it provides AI assistants secure access to workspace meeting data. The MCP tools return meeting content and structured meeting-related information.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth protection is observed on the endpoint and described in the integration guide. Workspace-level authorization and documented tool constraints are described, but no implementation code is public to verify them. Human confirmation is recommended for the client and is not documented as server-enforced. Encryption, retention, training, and employee-access claims apply to Krisp's broader meeting service; the reviewed sources do not establish MCP-specific enforcement details.

contradictions: The integration guide instructs clients to fetch protected-resource metadata at https://mcp.krisp.ai/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, but the provided pre-fetched response for that path was HTTP 404. The root metadata URL https://mcp.krisp.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returned HTTP 200.

The authorization-server scopes_supported list includes subscription and extensive kagent scopes, while the official supported-tools page lists only the 18 meeting-assistant tools and no subscription or kagent tools. Advertised scopes do not establish that those capabilities are exposed by this MCP endpoint.
Claude's third-party connector directory lists 7 tools while Krisp's official supported-tools page lists 18; the Claude list is incomplete relative to the official page.
observations_for_research: The official tool documentation explicitly separates read tools from six workspace-changing tools and recommends that the AI client require human confirmation before those write calls.
The authorization server advertises a broader set of OAuth scopes than the meeting-assistant MCP tool list uses or documents.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, pages/INDEX.txt, all collected official pages and scripts, links_check.txt, and code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt. Official help articles were HTTP 403 in the local page capture, so they were opened in the browser and read there. No official source repository or package was listed. The official tools article is the basis for the complete action list; its descriptions do not publish parameter schemas. Reviewed third-party catalogues include Claude, MartechDB, INITE Atlas, mcp.so, Omniio, and Agent Discoverability; no extra native action names were verified. No pricing specific to MCP calls was found.
